_note: Post-match press questions. Context picks the pool: scored, missed (played, no goal, low rating), won, lost, benched, rumour, gaffer. Each answer has a tone (humble, cocky, funny, dig), effects on meters, and a quote for Monday's paper ({NAME}, {OPP}, {TEAM}).
journalists: Barry from the Supporters' Club Newsletter

scored.q: What a goal against {OPP}. Where does that rank in your career so far?

answers.text: "It's all about the team. The lads made it easy for me."
"Top of the list. Then again, it's still quite a short list."
"I was aiming for the corner flag, to be honest."

scored.q: The fans were singing your name. How did that feel?

answers.text: "Unreal. I'll never take that for granted."
"They'd better get used to it."
"Louder than they sing for some of the others, that's for sure."

scored.q: Talk us through the celebration. Was that planned?

answers.text: "No, it just happened. I mostly ran towards whoever looked happiest."
"I've been practising it in the mirror for weeks. It deserved a goal."
"It was meant to be a knee slide. It turned into a sort of apology on grass."

scored.q: Who are you dedicating that goal to?

answers.text: "My mum. She's driven me to more training sessions than the bus company."
"Gran. She promised me a fiver per goal and she's about to regret it."
"Myself, mainly. I did all the hard bits."

scored.q: Did you mean it, or was it a cross that went in?

answers.text: "Bit of both. I'll take the luck, I've earned some."
"Meant every inch. Check the replay, I looked at the keeper first."
"I'll tell you after the goal of the month vote closes."

scored.q: Your boots looked brand new today. Lucky pair?

answers.text: "They were a present from my family, so they had to score really."
"They're lucky now. Last week they were just painful."
"It's not the boots. It's the feet in the boots."

scored.q: You've been on a bit of a drought. Relief to finally get one?

answers.text: "Massive relief. The lads never stopped backing me."
"I'd started thinking about goalkeeping. Glad it didn't come to that."
"Funny how it comes when someone finally passes it to me."

scored.q: Their keeper said before the game you didn't worry him. Anything to say to him?

answers.text: "He's a good keeper. Today just went my way."
"Hope he's worrying now. He looked worried when he was picking it out the net."
"I've sent him a get-well-soon card. And a calendar of my goals."

scored.q: Is it true you've started doing yoga? Is that the secret?

answers.text: "It helps. Mostly it's just the work on the training ground."
"I can't touch my toes yet but I can touch the back of the net."
"The secret is I'm just better than I was. Write that down."

scored.q: You scored in the rain and then took your shirt off. Cold?

answers.text: "Freezing. I apologise to everyone who had to see that."
"I've lost all feeling. Worth it. Mum's already rung to tell me off."
"Had to give the cameras something. Fans pay good money."

scored.q: Did you hear the ref tell you to calm down after you scored?

answers.text: "Fair enough. I got carried away. I'll apologise."
"I thought he was asking for a selfie, if I'm honest."
"First thing he got right all afternoon."

scored.q: Your goal's gone viral online. Have you read the comments?

answers.text: "Never read the comments. Mum reads them and tells me the nice ones."
"Someone said I run like a startled deer. I've made it my profile picture."
"Seen them. They're all correct. Especially the ones calling me a genius."

scored.q: That's your first goal at this ground. Anything special about it?

answers.text: "The groundsman. He gave me a nod. That meant a lot."
"The away end has the best pies in the country and I'll be telling everyone."
"It'll be the first of many. They should name a stand after me."

missed.q: You had chances today. What went wrong?

answers.text: "I should have done better. I'll be back on the training ground Monday."
"The service wasn't great, if I'm honest."
"The goal moved. I've got video evidence."

missed.q: Some fans are saying you're not ready. Are they right?

answers.text: "I've got a lot to learn. I'll prove them wrong."
"Some fans also think the Earth is flat."
"I'm ready. I just didn't tell my legs."

missed.q: That miss in the second half. Have you seen it back yet?

answers.text: "I've seen it. I'll keep seeing it until I've fixed it."
"I'm told it's now a ringtone. Smashing."
"Nine times out of ten that's in. This was the tenth."

missed.q: Was the pitch to blame today? It looked heavy.

answers.text: "Same pitch for both teams. No excuses."
"I lost a boot in the six-yard box. If anyone finds it, it's a size nine."
"Ask the groundsman. Actually, ask whoever pays the groundsman."

missed.q: You were hooked just after the hour. Fair decision?

answers.text: "Completely fair. I wasn't at it today."
"I'd have liked longer. Some lads get the full ninety whatever they do."
"I'd run out of ideas and also out of breath, so good timing really."

missed.q: Your mum was in the stand. What's she going to say?

answers.text: "She'll say keep your head up. She always does."
"She'll say my hair looked nice. That's how I know it went badly."
"She'll say I was the best player on the pitch. Mums are always right."

missed.q: Did the wind get to you out there?

answers.text: "Everyone had the same wind. I need to adapt better."
"One of my crosses is still going. Probably over Belgium by now."
"Wind, ref, the lot. Nothing went our way, nothing."

missed.q: Is there something going on off the pitch? You looked distracted.

answers.text: "No, all good. Just an off day, they happen."
"I left the oven on. I'm almost sure of it. Still am."
"Distracted? I was saving myself for a big game."

missed.q: You've been posting a lot online lately. Is it affecting your football?

answers.text: "Fair question. I'll put the phone down for a bit."
"My last post was a picture of a sandwich. I don't think the sandwich is to blame."
"My followers don't seem bothered. Maybe you should follow me."

missed.q: That poor first touch kept letting you down. Anything wrong with the ball?

answers.text: "Nothing wrong with the ball. Plenty wrong with my touch. I'll sort it."
"The ball and I are on a break. We're talking it through."
"Ball was fine. Some of the passes coming at me were lethal though."

missed.q: Their full-back had you in his pocket. Did he say anything to you?

answers.text: "He played well. Credit where it's due."
"He kept asking where I got my headband. I didn't have the heart to say Gran knitted it."
"Enjoy it while it lasts. Next time I'll be in his nightmares."

missed.q: Your rating in the papers will be low. Bothered?

answers.text: "Deserved. I'll take it on the chin and go again."
"I'll frame it. Something to look back on when I'm a legend."
"Bit rich from people who've never kicked a ball. No offence."

missed.q: You skied that penalty. What happened?

answers.text: "Not good enough. I let the lads down and I'll make it up to them."
"I've always wanted to hit the moon. Nearly managed it."
"I'll be taking the next one. And I'll score it."

won.q: Big win. How's the mood in the dressing room?

answers.text: "Buzzing. Credit to the gaffer, he had us ready."
"Gaz is doing his dance. It's horrific. Send help."
"We'll beat anyone playing like that. Anyone."

won.q: You didn't score but you were everywhere. Satisfied?

answers.text: "I just do my job. The goals will come."
"I covered so much ground I've been charged for a second ticket."
"Satisfied? I carried that midfield. My back's sore."

won.q: Three points against {OPP}. Does that send a message?

answers.text: "It's one game. We stay humble and go again."
"Message sent, delivered and read. Two blue ticks."
"The message is: we're quite good when it doesn't rain."

won.q: What did the gaffer say at half-time?

answers.text: "He told us to be braver, and we were. Spot on."
"Something about a pike he once caught. Still not sure how it relates. It worked though."
"Honestly, we sorted it ourselves on the pitch."

won.q: Clean sheet as well. Credit to the defence?

answers.text: "All of it. The back line were brilliant. I just tried to help."
"Our keeper did a save with his face. He's now got a new face."
"I did a lot of defending myself, to be fair. Someone had to."

won.q: The travelling fans were incredible today. Any message for them?

answers.text: "Thank you. That journey's long and they still turned up singing."
"Whoever brought the inflatable banana: you're the real MVP."
"Keep coming. You're watching something special."

won.q: The ice bath must feel good after a win like that.

answers.text: "It's part of the job. Recovery matters."
"Nothing feels good in an ice bath. I made a noise I've never made before."
"I skip it. Some of us recover naturally."

won.q: What's the plan to celebrate tonight?

answers.text: "Early night. Big week coming."
"Gran's doing a roast. That's the party. It's a very good roast."
"Can't say. But keep an eye on social media."

won.q: The new kit's had some stick. Lucky charm now?

answers.text: "I'll wear whatever they give me. Proud to wear the badge."
"It looked like a deckchair until we won. Now it's a classic."
"It's growing on me. Unlike the training kit, which is growing mould."

won.q: The ref had a busy afternoon. Did he get the big calls right?

answers.text: "Refs have a tough job. He was fair to both sides."
"I've no idea. I spent most of the game trying to avoid his elbows."
"He got the result right, which was mostly in spite of himself."

won.q: You picked up a knock late on. Anything to worry about?

answers.text: "Should be fine. I'll do whatever the physio says."
"The physio said it's a bruise. Mum says it's a broken leg. We'll see who wins."
"I'll be fine. I'd play on one leg against this lot."

won.q: {TEAM} looked a different side today. What's changed?

answers.text: "Hard work in training. The gaffer's been on at us all week."
"We've switched to porridge. Never underestimate oats."
"A few of us finally got the shirts we should have had all along."

won.q: Who was your man of the match today?

answers.text: "Our keeper. Without him we're nowhere."
"The bloke selling programmes. He worked harder than anyone."
"Me. Obviously. Next question."

lost.q: Tough afternoon. Is the gaffer getting it wrong?

answers.text: "No chance. That's on us players."
"I'm not paid to pick the team. If I was, I'd be in it more."
"Honestly, I was just thinking about my tea."
"Fair. We need to look at ourselves."
"They wanted it more, they got it more. Basic maths."
"Some of us wanted it. Some of us were thinking about their hair."

lost.q: What do you say to the fans who travelled today?

answers.text: "Sorry. Simple as that. You deserved better."
"Sorry, and I'll pay for someone's chips. Not everyone's. One person's."
"Stick with us. I'll make it up to you personally."
"We can't hide behind that. We weren't good enough."
"If they have VAR here, it was hiding. I couldn't find it."
"Whoever was watching the screen must have been watching the snooker."

lost.q: You looked frustrated at the final whistle. What was said?

answers.text: "Just frustration. Nothing that leaves the dressing room."
"I said a word I'm not allowed to repeat in front of Gran."
"Some home truths. A few people needed to hear them."

lost.q: That's a few defeats now. Is there a crisis at {TEAM}?

answers.text: "No crisis. We stick together and work our way out."
"A crisis is when the tea urn breaks. This is just a bad run."
"There's no crisis while I'm here."

lost.q: The pitch looked like a ploughed field. Did it suit them more?

answers.text: "Same pitch for both sides. They handled it better."
"I saw a farmer looking at it with real interest."
"It suited their style. Their style being hoofing it."

lost.q: The referee gave very little your way. Thoughts?

answers.text: "He's got a hard job. We didn't do enough to make it easy."
"I'm not allowed to comment. My wallet's still sore from last time."
"He'll be in their club bar later, I'd imagine."

lost.q: How long until you can put this one behind you?

answers.text: "Tomorrow morning, in the gym. That's how you move on."
"Mum's lasagne usually does it in about forty minutes."
"Already have. I don't do sulking."

lost.q: The team bus got held up on the way here. Did that affect you?

answers.text: "No excuses. We were here in plenty of time."
"We spent forty minutes on the hard shoulder listening to the kit man's playlist. Scarred."
"Maybe the club could spring for a bus built this century."

lost.q: Do you think some of your teammates hid today?

answers.text: "No. We win together and lose together."
"Only Gaz, and he was hiding from his ex, who was in the stand."
"I won't name names. They know who they are."

lost.q: Was there a tactical problem today, playing that system?

answers.text: "The system's fine. We didn't carry it out."
"I'd tell you the system but I'd have to draw it, and I can't draw."
"Ask whoever drew it on the board. I think it was upside down."

lost.q: How do you pick yourself up for the next one?

answers.text: "Watch it back, learn from it, work harder."
"Ice bath, chips, sleep. In that order. Not at the same time."
"I don't need picking up. I'm already up."
"The gaffer picks the team. I'll keep working."
"Frustrated? I've been sat so long I've got splinters."
"I've got a lovely view from the bench. Best seat in the house."

benched.q: You made an impact off the bench. Point proved?

answers.text: "I just wanted to help the team. That's my job."
"Point proved, underlined, and laminated."
"Imagine what I'd do with ninety minutes. Someone should."

benched.q: What's it like warming up on the touchline for an hour?

answers.text: "You stay ready. You never know when you're needed."
"I've done that many lunges I've lunged into a new postcode."
"Lovely. I'm the fittest substitute in history."

benched.q: Did the gaffer explain why you weren't in the starting eleven?

answers.text: "He did, and I respect it. It's on me to change his mind."
"He did. It involved a long story about a trout. I think the trout was me."
"He tried. I'm still waiting for the bit that made sense."

benched.q: You only got ten minutes. Enough time to show what you can do?

answers.text: "Every minute counts. I'll take whatever I'm given."
"Ten minutes is enough to boil an egg. I just wanted to boil an egg."
"Ten minutes was plenty. Did you see that turn?"

benched.q: Are you worried about losing your place for good?

answers.text: "Competition's healthy. It pushes everyone."
"My place on the bench is very secure, thanks for asking."
"No. They need me, they just haven't realised yet."

benched.q: It was freezing out there. How did you keep warm on the bench?

answers.text: "Kept moving, kept focused. Same as always."
"Gran knitted me a bench blanket. With my name on it. In sequins."
"Some of us were sat out there long enough to know."

benched.q: Your family came to watch and you only played the last few minutes. Disappointed for them?

answers.text: "They'll be proud I got on. They always are."
"Mum saw me take my tracksuit off and cheered like I'd scored. Bless her."
"I'd love to have shown them more. Maybe next time, eh gaffer?"

benched.q: You came on and the first thing you did was concede a free kick. Rusty?

answers.text: "Little bit, yeah. Game time sorts that out."
"My legs had gone to sleep. They woke up angry."
"Tactical foul. Read the game. Very clever, actually."

benched.q: The fans were chanting for you to come on. Did you hear them?

answers.text: "I did. It means the world. I'll repay them."
"I thought they were chanting for the pie man. Very flattering either way."
"Everyone heard them. Well, almost everyone."

benched.q: You were spotted chatting to the kit man all game. What about?

answers.text: "He's a good bloke. Been at the club years. You learn things."
"The best way to fold a towel. It's a three-part fold. Life-changing."
"Tactics. He's got some good ideas. Better than some."

benched.q: Would you consider a loan move to get regular football?

answers.text: "I'm focused here. I'll fight for my place."
"I've got a loan already. It's for a car that doesn't start."
"If someone's offering minutes, I'm listening."

benched.q: What do you actually do on the bench for an hour?

answers.text: "Watch, learn, see where I can hurt them when I come on."
"Count seagulls. Fourteen today. A personal best."
"Mostly I work out how I'd pick the team. It's quite different."

rumour.q: There's talk of bigger clubs watching you. Would you be tempted?

answers.text: "I'm happy here. I just want to play."
"Never say never. My agent's got a fax machine."
"The only club I'm joining is Gran's bingo club."

rumour.q: A scout from a big club was in the stand today. Did you know?

answers.text: "I didn't. I just play for the badge."
"I thought he was the bloke from the gas board. He had a clipboard."
"Hope he enjoyed the show. Tickets for the next one are going fast."

rumour.q: Would you kiss the badge to calm the fans' nerves?

answers.text: "I'd rather show them with my performances than with a kiss."
"I kissed it once and got a mouthful of fabric softener. Never again."
"I'll kiss whatever badge is on my shirt at the time."

rumour.q: Your agent was seen having lunch with another club's director. Anything in it?

answers.text: "He has lunch with everyone. I'm focused on the next game."
"He'll have lunch with anyone. He once had lunch with my dentist."
"I'd be worried if he wasn't having lunch with people."

rumour.q: A paper says you've already agreed personal terms elsewhere. True?

answers.text: "Rubbish. Not true at all. I'm going nowhere."
"The only terms I've agreed are with Mum, about doing the washing up."
"Whoever wrote that should stick to the horoscopes."

rumour.q: What would it take to keep you at {TEAM}?

answers.text: "Nothing. I love it here. That's the honest answer."
"A parking space closer to the door. And biscuits in the canteen. The good ones."
"A bit more ambition from upstairs wouldn't hurt."

rumour.q: Have you spoken to your family about a possible move?

answers.text: "Family come first. Right now we're all happy where we are."
"Gran says she's not moving anywhere that hasn't got her chippy."
"They'll go wherever I go. They know which way the wind's blowing."

rumour.q: Fans are worried you'll be gone by the end of the window. What do you say to them?

answers.text: "Don't worry. I'm committed to this club."
"I've just bought a season ticket for my mum. I'm not wasting that."
"Enjoy me while you've got me."

rumour.q: Is it true you've been learning a foreign language?

answers.text: "Only so I can talk to our new signing. He's a lovely lad."
"I can say 'one more chips please' in four languages. That's it."
"Let's just say it might come in handy. Adiós."

rumour.q: Your social media has just started following a rival club. Explain?

answers.text: "Pure accident. My thumb's got a mind of its own. Sorry, everyone."
"That was my little cousin. He's been banned from my phone. And from Christmas."
"I follow lots of things. Read into it what you like."

rumour.q: After today's performance, is your price going up?

answers.text: "I don't think about price. I think about the next game."
"Last I checked I was worth about three Freddos and a bus pass."
"I'd hope so. Quality costs."

rumour.q: A big club's manager called you 'one to watch'. Flattered?

answers.text: "It's nice, but it's my own gaffer's opinion that matters."
"I've been 'one to watch' since primary school. Mainly by dinner ladies."
"Nice to be appreciated somewhere, isn't it."

rumour.q: If the right offer came in, would you push for a move?

answers.text: "I'd never push. I'd only ever leave the right way."
"I can't even push a trolley in a straight line. No chance."
"I'd at least push the door open and have a look."

gaffer.q: What's the gaffer like to work for?

answers.text: "He's taught me loads. Mostly about fish, but loads."
"Bit old school. Thinks a tactics board is for drawing trout."
"Don't get him started on carp. Seriously. Don't."

gaffer.q: Is it true you and the gaffer had words at training this week?

answers.text: "We talk all the time. He wants the best for me."
"We did. The words were 'tench' and 'tackle'. It was about fishing."
"He had words. I had better ones."

gaffer.q: Would you say you're one of the gaffer's favourites?

answers.text: "He treats everyone the same. That's why the lads respect him."
"He gave me a maggot once. I think that's a sign of affection."
"I'd be everyone's favourite if they had any taste."

gaffer.q: The gaffer's under pressure. Do the players still back him?

answers.text: "One hundred percent. We're playing for him."
"We back him. We'd back him even more if he stopped bringing bait to the canteen."
"You'd have to ask the players. I'm only one of them."

gaffer.q: What's the best bit of advice the gaffer's ever given you?

answers.text: "'Do the simple things well.' I think about it every game."
"'Never trust a man who doesn't own a flask.' Not football, but true."
"Still waiting for it, to be honest."

gaffer.q: The gaffer's tactics have been called boring. Fair?

answers.text: "Boring wins games. I'm happy with boring."
"He'd call it 'patient'. Like fishing. He calls everything like fishing."
"I've had more excitement watching a kettle boil."

gaffer.q: How does the gaffer react after a defeat?

answers.text: "Calm. He tells us what went wrong and we fix it."
"He goes very quiet and stares at a photo of a large pike."
"Throws a teacup. Usually near me. I'm sure that's coincidence."

gaffer.q: Have you been round to the gaffer's house?

answers.text: "Once, for a team barbecue. Lovely family."
"Yes. There's a fish tank in every room. Including the loo."
"No, but he's always welcome round mine. Bigger telly."

gaffer.q: Does the gaffer give a good team talk?

answers.text: "The best. He knows exactly what to say."
"Last one lasted twenty minutes and only six of those were about football."
"When he's awake for it, yeah."

gaffer.q: Would you like to be a manager yourself one day?

answers.text: "Maybe. I'd want to be like ours. He's taught me a lot."
"Only if I can wear a big coat and shout at a fourth official."
"I'd be good at it. Couldn't be much worse than some I've seen."

gaffer.q: The gaffer's been seen in the same tracksuit for three weeks. Should someone say something?

answers.text: "If it works for him, it works for us."
"It's a lucky tracksuit. It can now stand up on its own. We don't ask."
"Someone should say something. Ideally the laundry."

gaffer.q: Is the gaffer strict about diet?

answers.text: "Very. And he's right. I feel the difference."
"No chips. Except Fridays. Except when we win. So no chips."
"Strict for us. He had a bacon roll at half-time."

gaffer.q: Does the gaffer understand modern football?

answers.text: "He's sharper than people think. Trust me."
"He's just discovered emojis. He only uses the fish one, but it's a start."
"He thinks 'pressing' is something you do to trousers."
